items.description:
Security forces conducted an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Muzak village, on the southern outskirts of Mir Ali in North Waziristan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, neutralising two terrorist hideouts, the military’s media wing said on Monday.

items.title: UN chief urges leaders to ‘get serious’ as COP31 set to open
items.description:
United Nations chief Antonio Guterres urged world leaders on Monday to “get serious” about tackling climate change as the COP31 conference was set to open with negotiators already tangled in an early fight over money.
Guterres made his plea as thousands of participants descended on a sprawling expo centre in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya for the UN’s annual climate talks.
The summit comes after a year of punishing heatwaves in Europe, major wildfires in Indonesia and catastrophic floods in Nepal, with an exceptionally strong El Nino weather phenomenon fuelling more climate chaos.

items.title: Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport in clearest sign of plans to return to Bangladesh
items.description:
Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina requested on Monday a new passport and identity card so she can return from self-imposed exile in India, according to a letter seen by Reuters, her first such communication since fleeing in 2024.
The request marks the clearest step by Hasina to act on her plan to return to Bangladesh in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising ended her long rule, raising the prospect of fresh political and legal tensions in a country where her party is now banned.

items.title: Iqbal and the Pakistani dream: fact or fiction?
items.description:
Visiting Srinagar once, Indian essayist Pankaj Mishra found Iqbal in a rather unexpected place. Or, at least, in an unlikely heart.
For most Indians, Mishra notes, Iqbal was simply the “misguided instigator of the movement for Pakistan.” But then Mishra met Mohammad Ishaq Khan, a historian of Islam in Kashmir. By his very nature, Dr. Khan held politics at arm’s length; his writing focused on faith’s quieter, more contemplative hues.

items.title: Bangladesh's external debt increases almost threefold in decade
items.description:
Bangladesh’s foreign debt has almost tripled in 10 years, a steeper rise than in any other South Asian country except the Maldives, according to the World Bank.
Even so, the country has a lower debt burden relative to export earnings than Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Bhutan. However, its burden is higher than that of India and Nepal.

items.title: Historical gurdwara on Lahore's Temple Road reopens first time since Partition
items.description:
LAHORE: The historical Gurdwara Chhevin Patshahi Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib on Temple Road, Mozang, which had been closed since the Partition, was reopened here on Sunday after completion of its restoration. The Evacuee Trust Property Board, Pakistan Sikh Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (PSGPC) and the Punjab government held a joint ceremony to mark its reopening after 79 years.
